introduction: ERC-7683 defines a standard interface for cross-chain trade intents. Users express their desired outcome (e.g., swap USDC on Ethereum for USDC on Optimism) as an order, and competitive fillers race to fulfill these orders on the destination chain. The standard specifies how orders are opened on the origin chain, filled on the destination chain, and settled through a resolution mechanism. It supports both on-chain orders and gasless (signature-based) orders.
designPurpose: ERC-7683 was designed to standardize the fragmented cross-chain bridging landscape. Each bridge protocol had its own proprietary order format and settlement mechanism, creating liquidity fragmentation and poor user experience. By defining a common cross-chain order interface, ERC-7683 enables fillers to operate across multiple settlement systems and users to benefit from competitive filling regardless of which settlement protocol is used.
commonUsage: ERC-7683 is used by cross-chain intent protocols like UniswapX, Across Protocol, and other bridge aggregators. It enables users to express cross-chain swaps as intents that are competitively filled by market makers. The standard is particularly useful for cross-chain token transfers, cross-chain swaps, and any operation that requires moving value between blockchains with minimal user friction.
fn.open.desc: Opens a new cross-chain order on the origin chain. Locks the user's input tokens and broadcasts the order for fillers to fulfill on the destination chain.
fn.open.params.order: The OnchainCrossChainOrder struct containing fill deadline, order data type, and encoded order data.
fn.fill.desc: Fills a cross-chain order on the destination chain by delivering the output tokens to the user. The filler provides their own liquidity and will be reimbursed from the origin chain.
fn.fill.params.orderId: The unique identifier of the cross-chain order to fill.
fn.fill.params.originData: Encoded data from the origin chain needed to validate the fill.
fn.fill.params.fillerData: Filler-specific data, such as the filler's preferred repayment address.
fn.resolve.desc: Resolves a gasless cross-chain order by validating the user's signature and converting it into a resolved order with concrete input/output amounts.
fn.resolve.params.order: The GaslessCrossChainOrder struct containing the user's signed order parameters.
fn.resolve.params.sig: The user's EIP-712 signature authorizing the cross-chain order.
fn.resolve.params.originFillerData: Data from the filler on the origin chain.
fn.resolve.returns.resolvedOrder: The resolved order with concrete token amounts and addresses.
fn.GaslessCrossChainOrder.desc: Struct/event representing a gasless cross-chain order that is signed off-chain by the user and submitted by a filler.
fn.GaslessCrossChainOrder.params.originS: The settlement contract address on the origin chain.
fn.GaslessCrossChainOrder.params.user: The user who created and signed the order.
fn.GaslessCrossChainOrder.params.nonce: A unique nonce to prevent order replay.
fn.GaslessCrossChainOrder.params.originC: The chain ID of the origin chain.
fn.GaslessCrossChainOrder.params.openDea: The deadline by which the order must be opened on-chain.
fn.GaslessCrossChainOrder.params.fillDea: The deadline by which the order must be filled on the destination chain.
fn.GaslessCrossChainOrder.params.orderDa: A bytes32 identifier for the order data encoding format.
The encoded order-specific data (tokens, amounts, destination chain, etc.).
fn.OnchainCrossChainOrder.desc: Struct/event representing an on-chain cross-chain order submitted directly by the user via a transaction.
fn.OnchainCrossChainOrder.params.fillDea: The deadline by which the order must be filled.
fn.OnchainCrossChainOrder.params.orderDa: A bytes32 identifier for the order data encoding format.
sim.crossChainIntent.name: Cross-Chain Intent Flow
sim.crossChainIntent.desc: Execute a cross-chain token transfer using the intent-based settlement pattern.
sim.crossChainIntent.step.open: The user opens a cross-chain order on the origin chain. Their input tokens are locked in the settlement contract until the order is filled or expires.
sim.crossChainIntent.step.broadcast: The order is broadcast to fillers who monitor for profitable opportunities. Fillers compete to fill the order at the best price.
sim.crossChainIntent.step.fill: A filler fills the order on the destination chain by sending the output tokens directly to the user from their own liquidity.
sim.crossChainIntent.step.settle: The fill is proven to the origin chain via the resolver. The settlement contract releases the locked input tokens to the filler as reimbursement.
